title: Assurance Governance Policy
rationale: Single top-level policy: security objectives, roles, risk, compliance, internal control, exceptions, authority. TSC CC1-CC5, Safeguards 314.4(a)-(b),(i) all expect a documented program; one document avoids five overlapping ones.

title: Code of Conduct and Acceptable Use
rationale: Personnel must acknowledge conduct, conflicts and acceptable use; signature-bearing document is customary and auditor-expected (CC1.1). Kept separate because it is addressed to people, not systems.

title: People Security Policy
rationale: Onboarding, screening, training, offboarding; CC1.4, CC2.2, Safeguards 314.4(e).

title: Identity and Access Policy
rationale: Human, service and agent identities under one policy; CC6.1-6.3, Safeguards 314.4(c)(1),(c)(5).

title: Data Protection Policy
rationale: Classification, cryptography, retention/deletion, privacy, records, tenant isolation of data; CC6.1/6.7, C1, P-series, Safeguards 314.4(c)(2)-(3),(c)(6).

title: Secure Engineering and Change Policy
rationale: Entire SDLC and supply chain in one policy because the same pipeline enforces it; CC8.1, SSDF, SLSA, Safeguards 314.4(c)(4),(c)(7).

title: Operations Security Policy
rationale: Configuration, network, cloud, endpoint, vulnerability, testing, logging and monitoring; CC6.6-6.8, CC7.1-7.2, Safeguards 314.4(c)(8),(d).

title: Incident Response and Notification Policy
rationale: Incidents including AI incidents and breach/customer/regulator notification; CC7.3-7.5, Safeguards 314.4(h),(j), state breach laws.

title: Resilience Policy
rationale: Backup, continuity, disaster recovery, availability commitments; A1, CC9.1.

title: Third-Party and Vendor Risk Policy
rationale: Vendors, subservice organizations, AI/model providers, bank partners; CC9.2, Safeguards 314.4(f), interagency TPRM flow-down.

title: AI and Autonomous Systems Policy
rationale: Agents act inside every other policy; this policy fixes identity, authority, boundaries and accountability for agents once rather than repeating in each. NIST AI RMF GOVERN, ISO 42001 5.2.

title: Financial Operations Integrity Policy
rationale: Product-scoped (Unbound first): authorization, ledger integrity, reconciliation, fraud, corrections. Basis for any SOC 1 control objectives.

title: Customer Operations Policy
rationale: Customer onboarding/termination, configuration governance, complaints, notification, service commitments; CC2.3, CC3.4, A1.

title: Information security objectives, roles and responsibilities
rationale: Information security policy is the objective/role core of POL-01 rather than a separate document.

title: Risk management
rationale: Risk assessment method and register (CC3.1-3.4, Safeguards 314.4(b)).

title: Compliance management and requirement monitoring
rationale: Requirement register, change monitoring, applicability decisions.

title: Internal control and control lifecycle
rationale: Control catalog, status vocabulary, testing, deficiency handling (CC4, CC5).

title: Exception and risk acceptance management
rationale: Exception register with expiry, compensating control, approver independent of requester.

title: Delegation of authority
rationale: Who may approve what; machine-readable authority matrix consumed by enforcement.

title: Segregation of duties
rationale: Incompatible-duty matrix covering humans and agents; small-team compensating controls.

title: Policy lifecycle and document/records management
rationale: Policy versioning, approval, publication; records management folded here. Git history is the change record.

title: Management review and assurance reporting
rationale: Periodic review of control health metrics, risks, exceptions.

title: Ethics and conflicts of interest
rationale: Conflict disclosure, especially for financial approvers and related parties.

title: Acceptable use (systems and data)
rationale: Includes AI acceptable use for personnel; agent behavior is POL-11.

title: AI acceptable use for personnel
rationale: Which AI tools/providers personnel may use with which data classes.

title: Onboarding and screening
rationale: Background checks per role risk; access only after acknowledgement.

title: Security awareness and training
rationale: Role-based training; completion evidence generated by the training system.

title: Offboarding
rationale: Access revocation driven by HR event; same-day for privileged.

title: Identity lifecycle and access provisioning
rationale: Joiner/mover/leaver for humans, services and agents.

title: Privileged access
rationale: Just-in-time, time-bound, approved, logged; no standing production admin.

title: Authentication and MFA
rationale: Phishing-resistant MFA for all human access to systems with nonpublic information.

title: Password and credential management
rationale: Folded into authentication; separate password policy not needed when SSO+passkeys/MFA enforced (NIST SP 800-63B).

title: Secrets management
rationale: Secrets only in managed vault; short-lived workload identity preferred over static secrets.

title: Access review
rationale: Continuous entitlement diffing replaces most periodic manual review; periodic attestation retained for privileged roles.

title: Data classification and handling
rationale: Classes drive encryption, logging redaction, AI-provider eligibility, retention.

title: Encryption and key management
rationale: Managed KMS; encryption in transit and at rest; key rotation and access separation.

title: Data retention, deletion and legal hold
rationale: Includes financial record retention requirements (IRS, contract) and crypto-shredding for append-only stores.

title: Privacy management
rationale: GLBA privacy (as service provider), state laws, notices, data subject requests where applicable.

title: Customer (tenant) data isolation
rationale: Data-layer tenant isolation obligations; tests in TEN controls.

title: Financial record retention
rationale: Retention schedule for ledger, grant, contribution and tax records.

title: Secure software development lifecycle
rationale: SSDF-aligned practices; threat modeling for material changes.

title: Change management, code review and release
rationale: Change, code review and release management merged: one pipeline enforces all three.

title: Emergency changes
rationale: Break-glass path with mandatory retrospective review within defined window.

title: Dependency, supply chain, artifact signing and provenance
rationale: SBOM, pinned dependencies, signed builds, SLSA provenance.

title: Testing requirements
rationale: Mandatory tests including negative security and property tests; Echelon mandatory-testing principle.

title: Environment segregation and production access
rationale: Separate accounts/projects; no developer write access to production data.

title: Architecture governance
rationale: ADRs for new infrastructure, data categories, external APIs, autonomous permissions.

title: Infrastructure configuration as code
rationale: All infrastructure via reviewed IaC; drift detection.

title: Third-party software and service approval
rationale: Approval of new dependencies/SaaS linked to POL-10 for vendors with data access.

title: Configuration management
rationale: Baselines expressed as policy-as-code; drift detection.

title: Network and cloud security
rationale: Network and cloud combined: managed-service architecture makes them one control surface.

title: Endpoint security
rationale: Managed devices, disk encryption, OS updates, EDR per risk.

title: Vulnerability management
rationale: Scanning, SLA by severity, exception path.

title: Penetration testing and security testing
rationale: Risk-based internal and independent external testing; never represent scans as pen tests.

title: Logging, audit trails and security monitoring
rationale: Logging and monitoring merged; includes missing-log heartbeat detection.

title: Physical security responsibilities
rationale: Inherited from cloud providers (carve-out) plus remote-work device/premises rules; separate physical security policy not needed absent offices/datacenters.

title: Incident response
rationale: Detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned.

title: AI incident response
rationale: Agent misbehavior, prompt injection, model/provider incidents; kill switch.

title: Breach, regulator and customer notification
rationale: Deadlines by law/contract (e.g. FTC Safeguards 30-day notice for 500+ consumers, state laws, bank contracts).

title: Backup and recovery
rationale: Backup with tested restoration; restore tests generate evidence.

title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
rationale: BC and DR merged for a small, cloud-hosted organization.

title: Service availability
rationale: Availability objectives and capacity; links to customer commitments.

title: Vendor and subservice organization management
rationale: Inventory, due diligence, SOC report review incl. CUEC mapping, contracts, monitoring.

title: AI model and provider risk management
rationale: Provider data-use terms, retention, residency, fallback.

title: Bank and financial institution partner management
rationale: Obligations flowing down from bank partners.

title: Agent identity, authorization and credentials
rationale: Every agent has distinct identity, least privilege, short-lived credentials.

title: Agent execution boundaries and human approval
rationale: Actions agents may never take; actions needing human approval.

title: AI-generated code governance
rationale: AI-authored changes go through the same review/test gates with provenance marked; no self-approval.

title: Prompt injection and untrusted input
rationale: Technical objective: treat retrieved content as data; tool permission isolation.

title: AI data handling
rationale: Data classes permitted per provider; no confidential evidence to unapproved providers.

title: AI-generated evidence validation and autonomous remediation
rationale: Agent outputs are not evidence of effectiveness without independent validation; bounded remediation.

title: Agent accountability and model evaluation/monitoring
rationale: Named human accountable per agent; evaluation before deployment and drift monitoring.

title: Financial transaction authorization
rationale: Authority thresholds enforced in code; dual control above threshold.

title: Accounting integrity
rationale: Double-entry invariants, immutable posting, period close.

title: Reconciliation
rationale: Independent-source reconciliation (bank, custodian) with break management.

title: Fraud prevention
rationale: Fraud detection, OFAC screening, charity eligibility checks.

title: Transaction reversals, corrections and manual adjustments
rationale: Corrections only via compensating entries with approval; no history rewriting.

title: Customer onboarding and termination
rationale: Tenant provisioning, data return/deletion on exit.

title: Customer configuration governance
rationale: Tenant-specific policy changes approved by customer authority; versioned.

title: Customer complaints
rationale: Intake, tracking, root cause; required by some bank partner contracts.

title: Customer notification and communications
rationale: System changes, incidents, commitments (CC2.3).
